survey: A cartoon rocket flying diagonally up and to the right against a blue sunburst. Main parts: (1) a red ogive nose cone that sits on the silver body, with a red rolled rim covering the joint; (2) a silver cylindrical body that tapers a little toward the tail, with two round blue portholes in bronze rims set in a line on the side facing the camera; (3) two red flat fins at the lower body, one on each side, both joined flush to the hull. A third or fourth fin would be hidden behind the body from this angle. The left fin faces the camera more and the right fin is turned further away, which matches the rotation of the body; (4) a black ring nozzle at the tail, narrower than the body; (5) a small yellow exhaust flame coming straight out of the nozzle along the rocket's axis. The rocket is in flight, so it has no ground support and needs none. The flame is a real rocket feature, not an invented part. Every part joins the hull cleanly: nothing passes through anything else, the round parts are round, the counts are plausible, and the simplified shape could fly.
